Spheroidal coordinates ​

See also

Theory: Ellipsoidal coordinates · Curvilinear differential calculus · Spheroidal harmonics and their re-expansion

Manual: Coordinate systems (symbolic) · Charts and coordinate conversions · Spheroidal harmonics

Tutorials: The spheroid in spheroidal coordinates · Ellipsoidal coordinates · Changing the focal distance of spheroidal harmonics

A spheroid is an ellipsoid of revolution. The spheroidal coordinates are the orthogonal system in which a family of confocal spheroids is a family of coordinate surfaces: the natural system for a spheroidal inclusion, a penny-shaped crack or a needle. This page builds the prolate and the oblate systems with the steps of Curvilinear differential calculus, then writes their differential operators and the geometry of a spheroid seen as a surface. The notation is that of the appendix of Barthélémy and Bignonnet (2020).
